Toy multiSimmap of a categorical trait: stochastic maps of the colors

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_multiSimmap.Rd

Set of 10 stochastic character maps (multiSimmap) of phylograftR::toy_backbone for the colors of phylograftR::toy_tip_data ("blue", "green" and "red"). Each map is one possible history of the color along the branches, so that together they account for the uncertainty in the reconstruction of the ancestral states, unlike a single simmap. All the maps have the same states at the tips (the observed ones) and differ in the internal branches.

They were inferred from the tip data with deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data() (see vignette("prepare_stochastic_maps")): the models of equal rates ("ER"), symmetrical rates ("SYM") and all rates different ("ARD") were compared with their AICc. The best model was the equal-rates model ("ER"), under which the maps were simulated with phytools::make.simmap() (seed 1234). 100 maps were simulated, and only the first 10 are kept to keep the package light. 10 maps are enough for illustration, but actual analyses should use more maps (100 or more).

Usage

data(toy_multiSimmap)

Format

An object of classes "multiSimmap" and "multiPhylo": a list of 10 objects of class "simmap" (see phylograftR::toy_simmap for their structure), with the same tips, topology and branch lengths as phylograftR::toy_backbone. The class "multiSimmap" is what tells the grafting functions that the maps are alternative histories of the same trait (see vignette("prepare_stochastic_maps")).

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_tip_data for the tip data used to build the maps.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap for a single map of the same states.

  • phylograftR::toy_multiSimmap_elevation to combine with these maps as the maps of two traits.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa with the maps as constraints: each map is used for a different simulation.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_multiSimmap)
class(toy_multiSimmap)
#> [1] "multiSimmap" "multiPhylo" 
length(toy_multiSimmap)
#> [1] 10

# Plot the first two maps: two possible histories of the same trait
state_colors <- c(blue = "dodgerblue", green = "limegreen", red = "firebrick")
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap[[1]], colors = state_colors, fsize = 0.6, ftype = "i")
phytools::plotSimmap(toy_multiSimmap[[2]], colors = state_colors, fsize = 0.6, ftype = "i")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
